subject: Biology

stem: A cytogeneticist prepared a karyogram from a dividing cell of a female orangutan. The table summarizes five chromosome pairs.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Calculate the diploid chromosome number if the karyogram contains 24 homologous pairs.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Identify the evidence expected in the sex-chromosome pair for a female mammal.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Outline three steps used to produce a karyogram.

questions.title: Chromosome analysis

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Two chromosomes of similar size and banding pattern / two X chromosomes.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Arrest dividing cells at metaphase; stain/photograph condensed chromosomes; pair homologues using size, centromere position and banding pattern.

stem: Six quadrats were placed along an environmental gradient. Presence (+) or absence (-) of four grass species was recorded.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Suggest one abiotic factor, other than distance along the gradient, that may affect distribution.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain how a belt transect could provide quantitative abundance data.

questions.title: Habitat distribution and sampling

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Any one of soil moisture, temperature, light intensity, pH or wind exposure.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: The physical place/environment in which an organism, population or community lives.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Lay a tape along the gradient; place quadrats at fixed/random intervals; count individuals or estimate percentage cover in each quadrat and replicate transects.

stem: Equal masses of gelatin were incubated for 30 minutes with different protease concentrations. Soluble amino acid concentration was then measured.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Outline the relationship between protease concentration and amino acid concentration.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Compare the results at 20 degrees C and 35 degrees C.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Justify using soluble amino acid concentration as a measure of protease activity.

questions.title: Protease activity

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Amino acid concentration increases as protease concentration increases, then approaches a plateau.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Values are higher at 35 degrees C at every non-zero concentration; both treatments show diminishing increases at high concentration.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Protease hydrolyses peptide bonds; amino acids/short peptides are products; more product per unit time indicates a higher reaction rate, provided time, substrate mass and temperature are controlled.

stem: Yeast lawns were covered with different transparent materials, exposed to UV for four minutes, then incubated. Colony counts are shown.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Describe asexual reproduction by budding in yeast.

parts.label: b
parts.html: State one mutation type that UV can induce.

parts.label: c
parts.html: State one role of glucose in the agar.

parts.label: d
parts.html: (i) Explain the difference between the dark control and uncovered UV treatment.

parts.label: d
parts.html: (ii) Explain the difference between filters X and Y.

parts.label: e
parts.html: Evaluate the claim that fabric P is more protective than fabric Q.

questions.title: UV protection experiment

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: A small outgrowth forms; the nucleus divides by mitosis and one nucleus enters the bud before it separates.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Base substitution, deletion, insertion or frameshift.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Respiratory substrate / energy source / carbon source.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: (i) [1] UV damages DNA/kills cells in the uncovered treatment, so fewer colonies form.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: (ii) [1] Filter Y blocks/absorbs more UV than X, allowing more cells to survive.

solparts.label: e
solparts.html: P has a higher colony count, supporting greater protection; however, no replicate/error data are supplied, so reliability/significance cannot be assessed.
